desktopCoverage.interpretation: Coverage decodes the same repository UI Map, exposes structural labels for same-title states, and retains the actual title for replay and targeted exploration.

regressionsFoundInTapp: The final exploration action could end without emitting its destination state or transition; terminal transition resolution now reads the real final tree.
Directed native exploration performed a global tab sweep after reaching its target and could immediately navigate away; target runs now preserve the target budget.
Autonomous iOS exploration activated an existing app session and inherited stale foreground state; it now terminates and launches with the configured arguments and environment.
The UI Map keyed states only by visible title and collapsed structurally distinct list/detail/dialog states; stable evidence-grounded state variants now preserve them.
The native harness suppressed transitions when source and destination titles matched; structural hash changes now emit the transition with from/to hashes.
Task/contract grounding normalized a variant reference but not the map semantic key; both sides now use the same semantic normalization.
interpretation: Tapp now has a real native state-changing release contract composed from reusable Tasks over an evidence-grounded UI Map. It proves substantially more than reachability and replays deterministically without AI.
limits: The contract and three new Tasks were hand-authored and reviewed from observed evidence; autonomous business-plan generation did not produce them.
The fixture uses one deterministic representative title rather than a general collision-safe data generator and teardown policy.
This is single-actor local iOS simulator proof. Isolated native multi-actor sessions remain unsupported.
Android was not re-audited because adb was unavailable on this host.
The contract was not executed through a GitHub-hosted macOS Action runner.
